html:
SMTO-EML-0005 — Your mail server didn't accept SMTO's sign-in

GUID: ac52c664-8b67-5538-9553-26db20d4591a
Slug: email-authentication-failed
Domain: EML · Subsystem: email-smtp

What happened

  • SMTO reached your mail server, but the server refused the email account's sign-in, or SMTO had no sign-in details to offer. No email was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu, select your email sender profile, choose Reveal & edit value, check the username, and re-enter the current password or app password. Then select Save. An old or mistyped password is the most common reason a mail server refuses the sign-in.
  2. If the profile signs in with a Microsoft 365 or Google account instead of a password, ask SMTO to connect the email account again and select Open authorization page when it appears. The account's permission to send email may have expired or been withdrawn and needs to be granted again.
  3. Ask your email provider or IT team to confirm that sending through SMTP (sometimes called authenticated SMTP) is turned on for this mailbox. Many providers block this kind of sign-in by default, even when the password is correct.
  4. Ask SMTO in a conversation to test the email connection for that sender profile. The test signs in without sending any email, so you can confirm the fix safely.

What success looks like

  • The connection test reports the mail server is ready, and your next email is accepted.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your email account; the details include the server's response code. Never paste your password or a sign-in code into the chat or the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SMTP authentication failed before MAIL FROM: no credential was available for an authenticated profile, the server rejected AUTH (SMTPAuthenticationError or a non-235 reply), or the required SASL mechanism was not offered.

What this means

  • Authenticated sending has no credential to use, or the SMTP server raises SMTPAuthenticationError. Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.

Why this can happen

  • Authenticated sending has no credential to use, or the SMTP server raises SMTPAuthenticationError.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish absent private credentials from a numeric server authentication rejection and check the selected mailbox policy.

How to fix it

  • Check smtp_response_code and error_ref in the send result: 535 means rejected credentials, 454 a temporary failure, 432 or 534 an unavailable mechanism, 538 encryption required. Update auth.password (or the app password) in the email_smtp profile, confirm the mailbox allows SMTP AUTH, and for OAuth profiles re-authorize through the Auth broker (email.connect) with the required scopes; Email never requests tokens itself.
  • Check saved credentials, mailbox SMTP policy and scopes. OAuth reconnects through Auth; Email never requests tokens directly.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported private auth flow supplies valid scope and the intended server accepts authentication.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Only correlated SMTP stage and receipt evidence establish acceptance. An accepted message cannot be recalled by cancellation, and unknown delivery blocks automatic resend; diagnostic rendering sends no email.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
